papers.title: Trial emulation with observational data in cystic fibrosis.
papers.one_line: A cystic fibrosis position piece launches a registry-based emulation network whose stated first step is to reproduce existing trials in pre-modulator registry data so that later hypothetical emulations can be trusted, resting the whole program on an untheorized transfer from replication to new questions.
papers.what_was_done: The piece sets out the emulation workflow for cystic fibrosis registries: research question, target trial protocol covering eligibility, treatment strategies and assignment, follow-up, outcomes, causal contrast and analysis plan, then a mapping of each component onto observational data. The available resources are named with sizes, the US Cystic Fibrosis Foundation Patient Registry at about 32,000 individuals and the UK CF Registry at over 10,500 covering nearly the whole UK population, the latter cited in the NICE Real World Evidence Framework. Existing benchmarking programs are cited as precedent, including RCT DUPLICATE with 32 published trial emulations in US claims and the OPERAND project. The new CF Trial Emulation Network plans three stages: emulate existing trials in the pre-modulator era to see whether findings replicate and, where they do not, explore why; repeat those emulations in modulator-exposed populations; and then emulate hypothetical trials of combination therapy and treatment withdrawal for which no trial evidence exists. Named limits are confounding control, components such as dose and adherence that cannot be emulated exactly, and restriction to treatments already used in the population.

future_research.gap: Whether registry emulations reproduce trial results in cystic fibrosis, and why they differ when they do not, is unestablished
future_research.quote: A crucial step in establishing the potential of target trial emulation in CF will be to use registry data to emulate existing RCTs, to demonstrate the extent to which RCT findings can be replicated and identify sources of difference.

future_research.gap: Extending emulation to modulator-exposed populations, wider patient groups and hypothetical trials of combinations and withdrawal is planned but unvalidated
future_research.quote: Subsequent CF-TEN activities will include 1) repeating emulations of existing trials but in CFTR modulator-exposed populations

problems.evidence: The program's logic is stated as a conditional: success on trials that were actually run licenses belief in emulations of trials that were never run. Nothing connects the two. The trials available for replication were conducted before modulators became standard care, while the target questions concern long-term modulator effects, combination therapy and treatment withdrawal, which differ in confounding structure, comparator availability and follow-up length from the replicated set.
problems.quote: If findings from existing trials can be replicated, this will provide confidence that emulation of target trials that are hypothetical can provide reliable evidence about treatment effects.

problems.evidence: Replication is framed as a yes or no property of a comparison, the extent to which findings can be replicated, with the fallback of exploring reasons when they are not. No metric is proposed for how close two estimates must be, and no account is given of the estimand differences that will separate a registry emulation from a modulator trial with a fixed dose schedule and adjudicated spirometry endpoints.
problems.quote: to demonstrate whether the findings can be replicated for populations similar to those used in the original trial, and if not, to explore reasons for differences observed

problems.evidence: Dose and adherence are conceded as components that cannot be emulated exactly from registry records, which means the treatment strategy the emulation actually estimates is a class of dosing and adherence patterns observed in routine care rather than the protocolized regimen of the index trial. No procedure is proposed for deciding which observed patterns count as the same strategy, and this matters most for the planned combination-therapy and withdrawal questions where the strategy is defined by what is taken together and for how long.
problems.quote: Challenges include the ability to adequately control for confounding and that certain aspects of a target trial may not be possible to emulate exactly, such as specification of treatment dose, and adherence.

problems.evidence: The stated restriction, that emulation covers only treatments already used in the population of interest, is a positivity condition expressed as a program-level caveat rather than an analysis-level diagnostic. In a registry of 10,500 people where modulator eligibility is genotype-determined, the patient histories with no realistic probability of the comparator strategy are identifiable in advance, and nothing in the workflow requires them to be enumerated.
problems.quote: Trial emulation is also restricted to treatments that have been used within the populations of interest.

problems.evidence: Fitness of the UK CF Registry for effect estimation is established by citation, an appearance in the NICE Real World Evidence Framework as an example data source, and by coverage, nearly the whole UK population. Neither is a threshold on what the registry records about dose, adherence or the timing of measurements, and the same document concedes that those are the components that cannot be emulated exactly.
problems.quote: The UK CF Registry was highlighted in the NICE Real World Evidence Framework as an example data source for generating real-world evidence on effects of interventions.

papers.title: Random effects modelling versus logistic regression for the inclusion of cluster-level covariates in propensity score estimation: A Monte Carlo simulation and registry cohort analysis.
papers.one_line: Across 50 simulated scenarios and a knee replacement trial emulation, the propensity score specification that minimized bias flipped with cluster structure, with relative bias 24.5% for a random effects score versus 11.4% for logistic regression at 50 clusters of 200, and all six specifications gave overlapping intervals in the real registry.
papers.what_was_done: Monte Carlo simulations of about 10,000 individuals generated six patient-level covariates, two surgeon or hospital level confounders and a cross-level interaction, with 35 scenarios of 1,000 replications crossing five cluster structures from 10 clusters of 1,000 to 500 clusters of 20 and cluster-level confounding odds ratios from 1.01 to 2.5, plus 15 further scenarios with negative binomial cluster sizes. Six propensity score strategies were compared, logistic or random effects, each omitting cluster-level confounders, including them, or adding a cross-level interaction, with the treatment effect always estimated by a random effects outcome model weighted by stabilized inverse probability weights. Relative bias, mean square error and interval coverage were the metrics. At 50 clusters of 200 and confounding odds ratio 1.5 the random effects score gave 24.5% relative bias against 11.4% for logistic regression, while at 500 clusters of 20 and odds ratio 2.5 omitting cluster-level confounders gave 31.7% against 9.86% when they were included. The applied component used the UTMOST cohort of UK National Joint Registry knee replacements from 2009 to 2016 with 21,026 unicompartmental cases and 6,420 lead surgeons, outcome revision at 5 years, benchmarked against the TOPKAT trial. All six strategies found higher revision risk after unicompartmental replacement with overlapping intervals, while TOPKAT found no significant difference.

future_research.gap: How the clustering structure of real data governs the accuracy of propensity score weighting is unresolved
future_research.quote: More research is needed on how different cluster structures affect PS weighting analysis.

problems.evidence: Six propensity score specifications are compared and the ranking reverses with cluster structure: omitting surgeon-level confounders is best at 10 clusters of 1,000 and worst at 500 clusters of 20, where relative bias falls from 31.7% to 9.86% when they are included. The specifications are left deliberately unnamed because the literature supplies no rule, so an applied study choosing one of the six has no defensible default and no obligation to show that its choice moved the estimate.
problems.quote: We decided not to name reference PS strategies M1–M6 in this paper because there is no clear guidance in the current literature.

problems.evidence: In the registry cohort of 6,420 lead surgeons, many surgeons performed only one of the two procedures, so every patient of such a surgeon has zero probability of the other treatment once surgeon is in the adjustment set. That is a structural failure of support located in identifiable patient histories, and it is reported as a difference between simulation and reality rather than as a positivity diagnostic naming which patients are unsupported.
problems.quote: Second, we found that many surgeons carried out only one type of treatment in the real-world clinical study.

problems.evidence: The trial estimate is used as a bias yardstick for six observational specifications, but TOPKAT was underpowered and its interval so wide that agreement could not discriminate between strategies whose simulated relative bias ranged from about 10% to 32%. A comparison that cannot separate a 10% from a 32% bias is not a calibrated comparison of estimands, and the applied result is reported as all six being not significantly different.
problems.quote: where observational versus trial-based estimates were compared as a proxy for bias

problems.evidence: The simulated data allocate treatment individually so both arms appear in every cluster, while the registry contains surgeons who deliver only one procedure and cluster sizes that do not follow the simulated Poisson distribution. Pooling across surgeons therefore averages over units that were effectively conducting different single-arm practices, and the difference between the simulated and observed cluster structure is precisely what made the simulation ranking fail to reproduce.
problems.quote: This discrepancy in results between our real-world clinical study and simulations also highlighted that the cluster structure of the data affected the accuracy and precision of results for PS weighting analysis.

problems.evidence: The emulated intervention is a surgical procedure delivered by 6,420 lead surgeons, and treatment is not assigned patient by patient in that setting: surgeon volume and surgeon preference determine the procedure, so the effective assignment unit is the operator rather than the patient. The simulation that motivated the recommended specification assumed individual allocation, which is exactly the assumption the surgical data violate.
problems.quote: However, in our simulation study, the treatment is allocated individually, meaning both treatments can appear in all clusters.

papers.title: Data Imputation for Clinical Trial Emulation: A Case Study on Impact of Intracranial Pressure Monitoring for Traumatic Brain Injury.
papers.one_line: A study labeled trial emulation imputed missing baseline covariates with MICE and estimated an inverse probability weighted average treatment effect of intracranial pressure monitoring on in-hospital mortality of -1.43% (95% CI -2.36%, -0.51%) in 60,640 severe traumatic brain injury records, with no target trial protocol and a time zero defined only for treated patients.
papers.what_was_done: Four multiple imputation strategies and a complete case analysis were compared on two semi-synthetic benchmarks (Twins with 64,240 subjects and 40 covariates; IHDP with 747 subjects and 25 covariates) using expected precision in the estimation of the average treatment effect, then the best strategy was carried into an applied analysis. The applied data were 572,185 National Trauma Data Bank records from 2017 to 2018; the eligibility criterion of total Glasgow Coma Scale score of 8 or less left 74,819, of whom 5,261 (7.03%) had no recorded treatment and 10,879 (14.54%) no recorded outcome and were deleted, leaving 60,640 with 13,951 (23.01%) monitored and 46,689 (76.99%) not. Among the analyzed patients, 21,810 (36.97%) had at least one missing covariate, with the highest single covariate missing rate 37%, all imputed under a missing at random assumption with five imputations. Stabilized inverse probability of treatment weights were built from a logistic propensity score on 18 expert-nominated confounders; the largest absolute standardized difference fell from 0.284 before weighting to 0.014 after. The estimated average treatment effect was -1.43% (95% CI -2.36%, -0.51%; p = 0.00238) against unadjusted mortality of 53.97% treated versus 56.34% untreated. No treatment strategy, follow-up rule, grace period or per-protocol contrast was specified, and index time was set at the start of monitoring for treated patients only.

future_research.gap: How missing data should be handled inside a causal analysis of routinely collected data is unsettled
future_research.quote: However, discussions on how to address this issue in causal analysis using observational data are still limited.

problems.evidence: Time zero is anchored to an event that only occurs in one arm: the start of monitoring. Untreated patients have no corresponding anchor, so the interval between admission and the counterfactual monitoring decision is unallocated, and 23.01% of the 60,640 patients carry a time origin the other 76.99% cannot have. Nothing in the analysis selects that origin by a stated, outcome-blind rule, and no alternative grid was tested against the -1.43% estimate.
problems.quote: The index time was defined as the time of starting ICP monitoring for treated patients.

problems.evidence: Missingness in 15 baseline variables affecting 36.97% of the analyzed cohort is repaired by chained equations under an assumed missing at random mechanism, and the diagnostic offered is that imputed and observed densities overlap. Whether a trauma variable is recorded is itself a function of injury severity and of what the emergency service could measure, so the recording process is prognostic rather than ancillary, yet it enters no causal diagram and no sensitivity analysis.
problems.quote: Multiple imputation is valid under the assumption of MAR that missing data are related to other available characteristics and are random conditional on other observed variables.

problems.evidence: Eligibility is a recorded Glasgow Coma Scale below 9, so a patient whose score was never entered is dropped rather than classified, and the same applies to the 5,261 records with no treatment field and the 10,879 with no outcome field. Nothing distinguishes a patient who failed the criterion from one whose score was not transcribed, and the 74,819 eligible are reported as if the criterion had been evaluated for everyone in the 572,185 record source.
problems.quote: Considering the inclusion criteria, only 74,819 patients with total GCS score less than 9 were included in the analysis.

problems.evidence: The entire support argument is a balance table: the largest absolute standardized difference after weighting is 0.014, which is presented as a perfect balance among all observed covariates. Balance after weighting says nothing about which patient profiles had a near-zero probability of monitoring; severe trauma patients in centers that monitor everyone and patients with contraindications are exactly the histories that carry no comparative information, and none are named.
problems.quote: However, all ASDs were below 0.1 in the imputed dataset by IPTW, with the largest single value being 0.014.

problems.evidence: The outcome model is a treatment-only regression on the weighted pseudo-population, chosen for simplicity, and the imputation model was picked on two semi-synthetic benchmarks whose ground truth exists only because the outcomes were generated. No doubly robust or alternative estimator is run on the trauma data, so the sensitivity of the -1.43% risk difference to the estimator itself is unmeasured.
problems.quote: For simplicity, we used the treatment-only regression model to estimate ATE.

problems.evidence: The work is presented as clinical trial emulation, and a causal claim about monitoring is drawn on that basis, yet none of the seven protocol components is specified: no treatment strategy with duration, no assignment procedure, no follow-up rule beyond discharge, no causal contrast. The label carries the inferential weight while the assumption burden of the design, in particular a one-armed time origin and 36.97% imputed covariates, is unchanged.
problems.quote: Finally we successfully draw a causal conclusion that ICP monitoring was associated with a significantly reduced risk of death compared with treatment without an ICP monitoring among severe TBI patients.

papers.title: Spillover benefit of pre-exposure prophylaxis for HIV prevention: evaluating the importance of effect modification using an agent-based model.
papers.one_line: A two-stage randomized trial was emulated inside an agent-based HIV model of 17,440 simulated men, and the spillover benefit of pre-exposure prophylaxis to untreated partners was 13 fewer infections per 100 agents in high-prevalence network components against 5 per 100 in low-prevalence ones.
papers.what_was_done: The TITAN agent-based model, calibrated by Latin hypercube sampling against race-specific incidence from a local cohort, represented 17,440 men who have sex with men aged 18 to 39 in the Atlanta area, with partner selection driven by race and drug use and per-act transmission probabilities of 1.38% for condomless receptive and 0.11% for insertive intercourse. Network components with at least three agents and at least one infected agent were randomized 1:1 to a prophylaxis allocation strategy or none, and within intervention components eligible agents were randomized to prophylaxis at 70% coverage; each simulated trial averaged 3,947 agents in about 800 components of average size 5. Identification rested on partial interference, stratified interference and Bernoulli allocation, with two-stage inverse probability weights conditional on a binary component-level modifier, averaged over 1,000 simulations with 95% simulation intervals. Cumulative 24-month incidence was 10% in control components, 9% among unassigned agents in intervention components and 1% among those assigned prophylaxis. Spillover was larger where component HIV prevalence or density was above the median and smaller where drug use or bridging potential was higher. The network was fixed at baseline with no dropout and 100% retention, and sensitivity analyses covered 30% coverage, adherence and discontinuation.

future_research.gap: Which interference set is correct for a sexual network is unresolved
future_research.quote: Future work should include an evaluation of different interference sets, for example, by considering an agent's partners, known as nearest neighbours

future_research.gap: Spillover estimation with networks that change over time has no available method
future_research.quote: In future work, we plan to develop an approach that allows for assessment of spillover with networks updated over time and incorporate assortative mixing by age, which may be more important in a dynamic sexual network.

problems.evidence: Interference is made the estimand rather than assumed away: a two-stage design randomizes components and then agents within them, partial and stratified interference are stated, and two-stage inverse probability weights deliver spillover contrasts of 13 versus 5 fewer infections per 100 agents by component prevalence. What it does not close is the choice of interference set and the realizability of the strategy. The set is taken to be the entire component, so one agent's assignment is allowed to affect every other agent in it, an assumption the discussion concedes is dubious for large or loosely connected components, and 70% coverage is imposed by the simulation rather than implementable by any actor.
problems.quote: We assume partial interference ; that is, an agent's outcome is influenced only by others in the same component, but no agents outside the component.

problems.evidence: The model is validated by comparing simulated output to observed race-specific incidence rates, that is, on distributional fidelity, and is then used to produce causal contrasts with simulation intervals. Its own statement is that the simulated networks do not reflect the real ones, yet the estimated spillover effects are read as guidance for tailoring delivery to the most at-risk components. Nothing establishes that a model calibrated to marginal incidence supports interventional contrasts that depend on network topology.
problems.quote: As such, this simulation does not reflect the true underlying sexual networks among MSM in the Atlanta metropolitan area and the simulated trial is not intended to recreate the HIV epidemic in this setting.

problems.evidence: Positivity is listed among the usual assumptions and never examined, although the design creates support problems by construction: components with fewer than three agents or no infected agent are excluded, about 13% of components contain only one uninfected agent, and average component size is 5 with a standard deviation of 3, so a 70% coverage allocation is not attainable in small components. No diagnostic reports which component configurations had no realized counterpart under the alternative allocation.
problems.quote: We make the usual additional assumptions required for causal inference (i.e. exchangeability, consistency and positivity)

problems.evidence: The network is frozen at baseline and retention is set to 100% not because that is realistic but because the available estimators cannot handle components that change during follow-up. Partnerships in this population form and dissolve continuously, so the treatment strategy is defined over a structure that does not exist, and the size of the resulting error is unknown; the alternative would require identification of allocation strategies in continuous time with an evolving interference structure.
problems.quote: These assumptions were necessary because the existing methods for evaluating spillover do not allow for time-varying components in the sexual network.

problems.evidence: The contrasts are produced in a synthetic population whose parameters were tuned to published local estimates, and the intended use is real allocation of prophylaxis in Atlanta. Moving from the simulated 3,947 agents to a real network compounds the calibration assumptions on top of the interference assumptions, and the required work is named as still to be done rather than accounted for in the reported simulation intervals.
problems.quote: Important extensions are required to understand real-world HIV transmission and to inform real-world PrEP allocation decisions, including simulation of dynamic sexual networks, along with more extensive calibration and validation studies.

papers.title: Mediterranean Diet and Cardiovascular Prevention: Why Analytical Observational Designs Do Support Causality and Not Only Associations.
papers.one_line: A cohort of 18,419 with 171 cardiovascular events assembled eight analytic strategies to argue causality for the Mediterranean diet, and the same exposure scored three ways gave risk reductions of 29%, 20% and 17% per standard deviation while an emulated per-protocol trial returned a hazard ratio of 0.38 (95% CI 0.16-0.91) against the PREDIMED trial's 0.42 (95% CI 0.24-0.63).
papers.what_was_done: The SUN cohort of Spanish university graduates enrolled from 1999 was reduced from 22,894 to 18,419 by excluding short follow-up, implausible energy intake and prevalent disease; over a mean 11.5 years, 171 blinded-adjudicated cardiovascular events accrued and 7.3% were lost to follow-up. Adherence was measured by a 136-item food frequency questionnaire scored three ways: the Mediterranean Diet Score using sex-specific medians, a modified score using tertiles and a different component list, and the 14-item MEDAS screener used in PREDIMED. One standard deviation gave a 29% risk reduction (95% CI 14-41%) for the first, 20% (95% CI 3-44%) for the second and 17% (95% CI 1-31%) for the third. Extreme categories of cumulative exposure gave a hazard ratio of 0.30 (95% CI 0.14-0.62) with an E-value of 6.12, and the rate advancement period was 7.9 years (95% CI 1.6-14.2). Residual confounding was probed by adding confounders one at a time, by 1,000 half-sample resamplings and by eight naive negative control outcomes. A per-protocol trial was emulated by assigning participants aged 55 or older to a simulated low-fat arm if fat intake stayed below 30% of calories, or to a simulated Mediterranean arm if fat exceeded 30% and MEDAS reached 8, updating the assignment at four follow-up waves and censoring at nonadherence, giving a hazard ratio of 0.38 (95% CI 0.16-0.91).

future_research.gap: The set of analytic procedures that would license causal language from nonrandomized nutritional data is not settled
future_research.quote: Instead, the tendency should be to encourage researchers to evaluate different statistical approaches, equal or analogous to the ones presented in this study or other procedures better suited to the studied hypotheses.

problems.evidence: Three scores intended to capture the same exposure differ in components, in cut points and in whether they rank within the cohort, and they return risk reductions of 29%, 20% and 17% per standard deviation. The attenuation is attributed to a property of the screener rather than resolved, so which set of dietary patterns constitutes the treatment remains a modeling choice that moves the estimate by nearly half.
problems.quote: The risk reduction observed for one SD increase was 20% (95% CI 3–44%) for the mMDS and 17% (95% CI 1–31%) for the MEDAS (only in the analysis restricted to participants above 40 years old at baseline).

problems.evidence: The emulated intervention is a dietary pattern, and arm membership is defined by a threshold on realized intake, fat below 30% of calories for the control and fat above 30% with a MEDAS of at least 8 for the treatment. Nothing states what act would place a person in an arm, who or what does the assigning, or what version of the diet is being compared, so the contrast is between people whose eating already met two arithmetic conditions rather than between two implementable strategies.
problems.quote: we assigned participants 55 years or older to a simulated low-fat diet if during follow-up they kept the goal of having a total fat intake below 30% of total calories, or to a simulated MedDiet intervention group if they kept total fat intake above 30% of calories and achieved a MEDAS score (the one used in PREDIMED intervention) ≥ 8

problems.evidence: Because randomization to a diet cannot be observed, arm membership is reconstructed from questionnaires collected at 4, 6, 10 and 14 years and reassigned at each wave. The resulting estimand is defined by the measurement schedule of the cohort, not by the trial: it contrasts people who kept satisfying a score threshold at four fixed dates, which is a different quantity from the PREDIMED per-protocol effect it is compared against, and the difference is not quantified.
problems.quote: We updated this allocation to the simulated MedDiet intervention group or the simulated low-fat diet control group with repeated follow-up information obtained at 4-, 6-, 10- and 14-year follow-up

problems.evidence: Participants are censored when they stop meeting the adherence definition and a hazard ratio of 0.38 (95% CI 0.16-0.91) is reported and set beside the trial's 0.42. Censoring at nonadherence makes the risk set at each time a selected subgroup, so the reported quantity is a hazard among survivors who still satisfied the score, not the per-protocol effect the comparison implies, and no weighting for the censoring is described.
problems.quote: This approach simulated the per-protocol analysis of a pragmatic trial and we censored participants when they stopped adhering to the intended intervention

problems.evidence: Eight naive negative control outcomes are run, including mammography or prostate testing, any doctor visit, sport and road injuries, cataract surgery, glaucoma and bronchitis, and their null results are reported alongside an E-value of 6.12 and a health consciousness index built from ten screening procedures. That is a usable panel of controls in a single workflow. It stops short of integration: the controls are not used to calibrate the primary hazard ratio, no negative control exposure is used, no validation subsample supports the food frequency measurement, and no threshold is stated at which a control signal would have overturned the causal claim.
problems.quote: to evaluate whether the observed association might be the result of some artifact or another potential bias, we adopted the approach known as negative controls

problems.evidence: Residual confounding is probed by adding one confounder at a time and reading the direction of movement, with a strengthening association taken as evidence against residual confounding. That inference holds only if the remaining violations act alone; measurement error in a 136-item questionnaire, loss to follow-up of 7.3% and selection of a highly educated cohort are all present at the same time, and each is answered in a separate paragraph rather than jointly.
problems.quote: Our observation was that the greater the number of potential confounders adjusted for, the stronger the inverse association found, which speaks against important residual confounding.

papers.title: Trial Emulation Methods.
papers.one_line: A nephrology appraisal guide walks through the seven target trial protocol components using a rosuvastatin versus atorvastatin emulation, and its operational advice reduces to a standardized mean difference below 10%, one negative control outcome, and a choice between two time zero conventions with no rule for choosing.
papers.what_was_done: The guide states the seven protocol components and illustrates each with an electronic health record study of rosuvastatin against atorvastatin for hematuria and proteinuria in treatment-naive adults between 2011 and 2019 who had at least one year of continuous engagement with the health system. Eligibility is required to use no information after time zero, and complete follow-up is named as a criterion that induces selection bias. Assignment is emulated by propensity score matching or inverse probability of treatment weighting, with balance declared at an absolute standardized mean difference below 10% and extreme weights handled by trimming or overlap weights. Two time zero conventions are offered, a single eligible time or nested trials at all eligible times. Outcomes are two confirmed laboratory measurements, and patients with no measurement during follow-up are counted as outcome-free; equal testing frequency between arms is checked as a guard against differential ascertainment. Only intention-to-treat effects are estimated, with per-protocol contrasts referred to g-methods or cloning, censoring and weighting. Residual confounding is checked with a single negative control outcome, urinary tract infection, which showed no difference.

future_research.gap: Trial evidence for kidney populations remains scarce and observational emulation is offered as the complement
future_research.quote: Increasing the number of RCTs in nephrology, as well as the representation of patients with kidney disease in trials outside nephrology, is critical to move the field forward.

problems.evidence: Two conventions for time zero are presented side by side, a single eligible time or a nested trial at every eligible time, and the guide moves straight to references without a criterion for choosing between them. The two conventions target different populations and different amounts of follow-up, so the choice is consequential, and an appraisal guide that lists both without an outcome-blind selection rule leaves the analyst free to decide after seeing results.
problems.quote: One of 2 approaches is typically used: (1) choosing a single eligible time zero (eg, the first eligible time or a randomly selected eligible time) or (2) emulating multiple nested trials using all eligible times.
problems.locator: The Start of the Follow-up (Time Zero)

problems.evidence: The outcome is defined by two positive laboratory tests, and everyone never tested is classified as outcome-free. That converts a measurement process into a binary phenotype with an assumed sensitivity of one among the untested, and the only safeguard offered is that testing frequency looked similar across arms. Equal testing rates constrain differential misclassification but leave the nondifferential error, and its attenuating effect on the estimate, unquantified.
problems.quote: Patients who did not have laboratory measurements for the outcomes during the follow-up were also included and considered as not developing the outcomes.

problems.evidence: Positivity enters the guide only as an inconvenience of weighting: people at the tails of the propensity score produce extreme weights, and the remedy offered is trimming or overlap weights. Both remedies change the population being estimated without recording which patient histories were removed, and the reported diagnostic remains a balance statistic, an absolute standardized mean difference below 10%, that a trimmed sample satisfies by construction.
problems.quote: assessed by standardized mean difference and absolute difference <10% is considered good balance

problems.evidence: A concrete negative control outcome is supplied and used: urinary tract infection, chosen to be unaffected by statin type but sensitive to general health, showed no difference between arms and is reported as reassurance. That is one instrument placed in a named workflow slot. What remains open is everything around it: no negative control exposure, no proxy or validation subsample, no calibration of the primary estimate against the control distribution, and no statement of how large a control signal would have stopped the analysis.
problems.quote: In our example, we chose urinary tract infection as an outcome that would not plausibly be affected by statin type but could detect differences in the general health of patients.

problems.evidence: The appraisal checklist mixes checks that can be run against data, such as covariate balance and equal laboratory testing frequency, with the assumption that carries the inference and cannot be checked, conditional exchangeability given measured covariates. Both are presented in the same list of common sources of bias, so a reader cannot tell which items were verified and which were assumed.
problems.quote: propensity score methods (which are designed to address confounding bias) require the assumption that there are no unmeasured differences between treatment groups, conditional on the observed covariates

problems.evidence: Matching and weighting are laid out with their trade-offs, limited generalizability against extreme weights, and the worked example simply uses weighting. No rule tells an analyst which to pick for a given question, and no expectation is set that a study report the estimate under both. The guidance that governs how nephrology readers appraise these studies therefore contains no requirement that the estimator choice be shown not to matter.
problems.quote: Two common methods include propensity score matching and inverse probability of treatment weighting (IPTW), where multivariable logistic regression is used to model the probability of receiving one treatment strategy compared to the other.

papers.title: Combined Conventional Synthetic Disease Modifying Therapy vs. Infliximab for Rheumatoid Arthritis: Emulating a Randomized Trial in Observational Data.
papers.one_line: An emulation of the SWEFOT trial in the same Swedish register screened 57,288 rheumatoid arthritis patients to reach 509 analyzable ones and returned an adjusted response ratio of 1.48 (95% CI 0.98-2.24) against the trial's 1.59 (95% CI 1.10-2.30), agreeing on the estimate while disagreeing on the significance verdict.
papers.what_was_done: The protocol of the pragmatic SWEFOT trial, run in the Swedish Rheumatology Quality Register between 2002 and 2005, was re-specified for register data from 2006 to April 2020 and registered as NCT05051137. Screening 57,288 register patients with rheumatoid arthritis and applying eligibility of disease activity above 3.2, methotrexate for more than 30 days and no other prior disease-modifying drug left 509 patients, 313 starting infliximab and 196 starting sulfasalazine with hydroxychloroquine. The primary outcome was a European Alliance of Associations for Rheumatology good response at 9 months, with treatment discontinuation before evaluation classified as nonresponse; 26% of the infliximab arm and 33% of the comparator arm discontinued, and among those still on treatment the response measurement was missing for 28% and 25% respectively, imputed with 30-fold fully conditional specification alongside smoking status which was 60% to 70% missing. Stabilized inverse probability weights ranged to 28.1 and were truncated at 10 for three patients. Observed good response was 39% versus 39% in the trial for infliximab and 28% versus 25% for the comparator; the crude ratio was 1.39 (95% CI 1.04-1.86) and the adjusted ratio 1.48 (95% CI 0.98-2.24) against 1.59 (95% CI 1.10-2.30). Relaxing eligibility to allow prior non-methotrexate drugs cut the adjusted ratio to 1.19 (95% CI 0.86-1.66).

future_research.gap: Emulating a trial with data from a different setting than the trial's own source population is unsolved
future_research.quote: Emulating a trial using real-world data from different settings would impose additional challenges for the emulation, requiring creative solutions to overcome them

problems.evidence: A national register holding 57,288 rheumatoid arthritis patients yields 509 analyzable ones, a retention of under 1%, and the binding constraint was the comparator arm because combination conventional therapy has become rare in practice. The consequence is visible in the result: the adjusted interval runs from 0.98 to 2.24, wide enough that the emulation cannot distinguish the trial's estimate from the null.
problems.quote: After screening 57,288 patients with RA identified in the SRQ, and applying the eligibility criteria we included 509 patients who initiated either infliximab ( N  = 313) or SSZ + HCQ ( N  = 196) between January 2006 and April 2020.

problems.evidence: The treatment definition for the comparator arm, allowing the two drugs to start up to 180 days apart, was chosen to reach a target sample size rather than to represent a clinical strategy, and the same feasibility loop set the eligibility criteria. The reported interval is then computed as if that protocol had been fixed in advance of contact with the data, when in fact the data determined it.
problems.quote: The decision to allow a sequential initiation of the two drugs within this time window encountered in clinical practice was based on feasibility analyses with the goal of achieving sample sizes of ~ 200 patients per arm.

problems.evidence: Draft eligibility and exposure definitions were run against the data, judged on sample size and covariate balance, and revised, after which one version was registered. The registration therefore records the surviving protocol and not the discarded drafts, their sample sizes or their balance, so a reader cannot see how many definitions were tried before 200 patients per arm was reached.
problems.quote: Draft definitions of exposure and eligibility criteria were applied to the available data for initial feasibility assessment of sample size and covariate balance, without analyzing the association between treatment and outcome, and were revised aiming for a sample size of 200+ patients per arm

problems.evidence: On the estimate the emulation and the trial agree, 1.48 against 1.59 with overlapping intervals; on the binary verdict they disagree, because the lower limit lands at 0.98. The same comparison is therefore a success or a failure depending on which summary is read, and no calibrated statement of how far apart the two estimands are is offered in place of the label.
problems.quote: Due to small sample size, the lower confidence limit reached 0.98 in our IPTW adjusted main results and would be interpreted as “no statistically significant difference between treatments” based on a binary hypothesis test, disagreeing with SWEFOT.

problems.evidence: Staying on protocol treatment is defined by ad hoc equivalences: infliximab episodes less than 90 days apart are merged, a switch to etanercept for safety within 90 days counts as continuing, and in the comparator arm a switch to cyclosporin A extends protocol treatment. Because discontinuation is scored as nonresponse for 26% and 33% of the two arms, these version equivalences directly determine the outcome, and each was set by judgment rather than by any procedure.
problems.quote: Mimicking SWEFOT, patients who stopped infliximab for safety reasons, and initiated etanercept within 90 days were considered to stay on treatment until the end of etanercept treatment.

problems.evidence: Eligibility criteria are relaxed one at a time and the effect on the estimate is reported, isolating protocol compromise from estimation: permitting a longer disease duration and prior non-methotrexate drugs moved the adjusted ratio from 1.48 to 1.19, while restricting the comparator to simultaneous initiation left it at 1.47. That is a measured mapping loss for the eligibility component. It does not separate scientific-target mismatch from the rest: nothing quantifies the gap between the estimand of interest and SWEFOT itself, nor the loss from nonresponder imputation for the 25% to 28% with no recorded response.
problems.quote: Relaxing the eligibility criteria unsurprisingly increased sample size but also lowered the contrast between infliximab and SSZ + HCQ especially after allowing a longer RA duration and prior use of non‐MTX DMARDs.

papers.title: Can Machine Learning from Real-World Data Support Drug Treatment Decisions? A Prediction Modeling Case for Direct Oral Anticoagulants.
papers.one_line: Random forests estimated individual treatment effects for rivaroxaban against apixaban in 29,901 German claims records and, when the resulting recommendations were scored by trial emulation, cut the composite event rate by 0.78 percentage points (95% CI -1.40 to -0.03) on a discrimination for benefit of 0.56 (95% CI 0.52 to 0.60).
papers.what_was_done: New initiators of rivaroxaban or apixaban with atrial fibrillation in a German statutory insurer between 2014 and 2018 formed a cohort of 29,901, split 3:2 into 17,722 for development and 12,179 for validation, with entry requiring at least three follow-up prescriptions and censoring at death or switch to a vitamin K antagonist. Binary events within 365 days were modeled by an X-learner over random forests with 29 candidate effect modifiers, weighting for inverse probability of censoring and applying propensity score weighting to the outcome probabilities; the stroke model used automated hyperparameter tuning with down-sampling to a 3:7 event ratio while the bleeding model used standard forests. A composite decision threshold was chosen in the training data as the value maximizing the emulated benefit. Incidence was 2.0% for stroke and 9.7% for major bleeding. Recommendations disagreed with observed prescribing for 47.6% of rivaroxaban users and 63.9% of apixaban users under the stroke model. Discrimination for benefit was 0.56 (95% CI 0.52-0.60) for stroke and 0.52 (95% CI 0.49-0.54) for bleeding; absolute risk reduction in the apixaban bucket was 1.69% (95% CI 0.39-2.97) and the emulated implementation gave an absolute risk difference of -0.78% (95% CI -1.40 to -0.03).

future_research.gap: How treatment-guiding individual effect models should be validated with limited events is unsettled
future_research.quote: Nevertheless, alternative methods (e.g., cross-validation or bootstrapping) could be used for other applications of our principle, especially with small samples.

problems.evidence: Individual effect estimates are built from 29 claims variables that omit over-the-counter and temporary co-medication, and dosing is assumed correct although underdosing is acknowledged as common; the paper attributes the bleeding model's near-chance performance of 0.52 to those missing variables. The response is a more flexible learner rather than better identification, and the output is a recommendation for a named patient, so the unidentified part of the contrast is delivered as personalized advice.
problems.quote: possibly because many co-medications (including temporary or over-the-counter drugs) were not available in the present variables

problems.evidence: The decision threshold that converts benefit scores into recommendations is selected in the training data by maximizing the emulated benefit itself, and hyperparameters are tuned automatically on down-sampled data. Tuning on the target quantity in the same data that produced the scores optimizes apparent performance, and the validation that follows is a single split-sample; the surviving discrimination for benefit of 0.56 with a lower limit of 0.52 is barely separated from chance.
problems.quote: We determined this decision threshold in the training data by dividing probabilities into deciles and chose the threshold maximizing the emulated benefit as if the model were implemented into regular care
problems.locator: Model development: Estimation of ITEs for treatment recommendations

problems.evidence: Cohort entry requires at least three follow-up prescriptions, a healthcare-use criterion evaluated with information that only exists after the index date. Everyone who died, switched or stopped early is excluded, so the analyzed 29,901 are selected on continued engagement, which is caused by both the drug tolerated and the outcomes at issue; the resulting collider selection sits underneath every benefit score and the -0.78% projected risk difference.
problems.quote: were followed up from their first DOAC prescription if they met the inclusion criterion of at least 3 follow-up prescriptions

problems.evidence: Overlap is checked once, as a marginal comparison of propensity score distributions across the two drugs, and is then treated as sufficient for weighting individual effects. Recommendations are nonetheless issued for named strata, including an 84-year-old with an Elixhauser score of 16 and renal disease, and precision cohorts are formed from the 25% most similar patients. Support in the joint covariate space of such a stratum is never assessed, and it is exactly there that overlap is scarcest.
problems.quote: Most importantly, the propensity scores for treatment allocation obtained from these variables showed substantial overlap, which is required for weighting ITEs to calculate benefit scores

problems.evidence: Two different learners are used for the two outcomes, a tuned forest for stroke and a standard forest for bleeding, on the ground that the arrangement was considered most suitable, with untuned variants relegated to sensitivity analyses whose effect on the headline -0.78% risk difference is not reported. Given a stroke incidence of 2.0%, down-sampling to a 3:7 event ratio is a consequential choice, and no requirement forces the estimator comparison into the primary result.
problems.quote: While this procedure was considered most suitable, sensitivity analyses included also standard (i.e., nontuned) random forests with raw and randomly down-sampled data.
problems.locator: Model development: Estimation of ITEs for treatment recommendations

problems.evidence: The emulated trial converts a within-cohort recommendation rule into a projected clinical utility for implementation in regular care, a population that differs from the one the model was fit in: continuously insured patients of one German insurer who persisted for three prescriptions on one of two drugs. That transport step adds a sampling assumption on top of the no-unmeasured-confounding assumption already carried by the benefit scores, and neither the interval on -0.78% nor any separate analysis accounts for it.
problems.quote: While an actual trial would be required to assess the impact (clinical utility), observational data can be used to project the clinical utility by trial emulation.
problems.locator: Model evaluation: Validation of personalized recommendations

papers.title: Oncology Drug Effectiveness from Electronic Health Record Data Calibrated Against RCT Evidence: The PARSIFAL Trial Emulation.
papers.one_line: An emulation of the PARSIFAL breast cancer trial in 1,886 oncology electronic health records returned a hazard ratio of 1.07 (95% CI 0.86-1.35) against the trial's 1.00 (95% CI 0.68-1.48) while three-year survival was 59% in practice versus 78% in the trial, and was declared concordant on a standardized difference threshold.
papers.what_was_done: Outpatient records from the US Oncology Network were used to compare first-line palbociclib with fulvestrant against palbociclib with letrozole in hormone-positive, HER-2 negative metastatic breast cancer, with treatment ascertained from same-day physician ordering and no confirmation that drugs were taken. Eligibility gave 1,886 women, 462 and 1,424 in the two arms, with median time since diagnosis of 4.8 years against 1.1 years. The outcome was all-cause death recorded in a structured vital status field. Missingness ran from 2% for body mass index to 28% for performance status and 63% for number of metastatic sites and was imputed under an assumed missing at random mechanism with 50 chained-equation datasets; 18 of the collected pre-exposure variables entered a Cox model, the rest being too infrequent for convergence. The adjusted hazard ratio was 1.07 (95% CI 0.86-1.35) against the trial's 1.00 (95% CI 0.68-1.48), with a crude 1.24 (95% CI 1.02-1.51), and agreement was judged by a standardized difference below 1.96. Three-year survival was 59.5% and 57.7% against 77.1% and 79.4% in the trial. Complete case analyses moved further from the trial result. Imaging and visit rates were compared as a surveillance proxy, with imaging frequency missing for about 83% of patients.

future_research.gap: The conditions under which oncology electronic health record emulations produce valid effect estimates are unknown
future_research.quote: As more RCT emulation studies with oncology EHR data are becoming available, we will gain confidence in RWE studies in oncology and will be able to differentiate how to conduct such studies and when they will likely be leading to valid findings.

problems.evidence: Concordance is declared on the relative scale while the absolute scale diverges by about 18 percentage points of three-year survival, 59% against 78%. A hazard ratio near one is easy to match in populations with different baseline hazards, so the agreement label carries almost no information about whether the two studies estimated the same quantity, and no decomposition separates population difference from bias.
problems.quote: Although the 3-year survival was meaningfully lower in clinical practice (59%) compared to the randomized trial (78%), the relative effect size was a hazard ratio (HR) of 1.07 (95% CI: 0.86–1.35), similar to the randomized trial (HR = 1.00; 95% CI: 0.68–1.48).

problems.evidence: The outcome that everything rests on is a provider-entered vital status field whose completeness was never evaluated, and it is used as an error-free binary indicator of death. Deaths occurring outside the network are the plausible failure, and they would be differential if one arm's patients leave network care sooner. The three-year survival gap of 18 percentage points against the trial is compatible with either real prognosis differences or outcome capture, and nothing in the analysis separates them.
problems.quote: The completeness of mortality data in the database has not been formally assessed.

problems.evidence: The data carry 63% missingness on a confounder, 28% on performance status, imaging frequency absent for about 83% of patients, unverified drug administration and unassessed death capture, and none of these triggers a stopping rule. Each is instead handled narratively by an assumption or a sensitivity analysis, and the study proceeds to a headline estimate; no stated threshold on any of these quantities would have made the source unfit.
problems.quote: Notably, imaging frequency data were missing in approximately 83% of patients in either study arm.

problems.evidence: Positivity is assessed by looking at the spread of the weights by treatment group. In this cohort the two arms differ sharply on prior disease course, median 4.8 against 1.1 years since diagnosis, so the patients with no realistic probability of one regimen are identifiable by history rather than by weight magnitude, and no such history is named as unsupported.
problems.quote: The distribution of IP weights was evaluated by treatment group to check for the presence of any practical positivity violations, which can result in extreme weights.

problems.evidence: Two devices for unmeasured confounding are actually run: rates of imaging and office visits per patient-day as a surveillance proxy, and a bias analysis stating that a confounder would need associations of 1.64 or 0.61 with both exposure and outcome to move the result past the interval. Both are reported and both were null or reassuring. They are not integrated into a workflow: the proxy itself is missing for about 83% of patients, no negative control outcome is used, no validation subsample calibrates the death or covariate capture, and no threshold is stated in advance.
problems.quote: To explore the possibility of differential surveillance, the mean rate of imaging procedures and office visits per patient-day were calculated by treatment group as a proxy for unmeasured confounding.

problems.evidence: Missingness is attributed to changing reporting standards across practices and is then treated as repairable by imputation, with practice identifiers added as predictors. Whether a metastatic site count or a performance status was recorded depends on how sick the patient was and how closely they were followed, so the recording process is prognostic; that 63% of the metastatic site variable is generated rather than observed, and that complete case analyses moved away from the trial result, show the mechanism is doing real work.
problems.quote: Missing values were present in five confounding variables: body mass index (BMI) (2%), tumor stage (6%), smoking status (11%), performance status (28%), and number of metastatic sites (63%).

papers.title: When emulating a trial, do as the trialists do: Missteps in estimating relative effectiveness of a SARS-CoV-2 vaccine booster dose
papers.one_line: A correspondence documents a published booster effectiveness study that invoked target trial emulation while assigning treatment before eligibility and leaving up to three months between eligibility and the start of follow-up, biasing the reported 19%, 52% and 83% effectiveness estimates downward.
papers.what_was_done: The critique concerns a Veterans Affairs study reporting relative effectiveness of an mRNA booster against omicron of 19% for confirmed infection, 52% for hospitalization and 83% for intensive care admission or death, described by its authors as a target trial emulation. Four defects are identified. Booster recipients between 22 September and 25 December 2021 were identified first and then matched to not-yet-boosted individuals, reversing the order of eligibility and assignment. Follow-up began on 1 January 2022 for everyone, so pairs had to remain infection-free for up to three months to enter the analysis, which both selects on an unmeasured protective factor among the unboosted and discards early boosted person-time when effectiveness is highest, in a trial where no waiting period would exist. Controls who received a booster during follow-up were censored with no weighting for informative censoring. Pairs were matched on sex, age and comorbidity but analyzed without pair-stratified regression, so the interactions among matching factors that jointly determine COVID outcomes were not controlled. No target trial was defined in the original report.

problems.evidence: The original study invoked the framework by name and cited its founding papers, and that invocation is what a reader was offered as assurance against immortal time and selection bias. The correspondence shows the protocol was never written: treatment preceded eligibility, follow-up began three months late, and censoring went unweighted. The label was present and the assumption burden was untouched, which is exactly why the label cannot function as evidence.
problems.quote: Unfortunately, the authors did not define or adhere to the target trial they sought to emulate, leading to several study design and analysis concerns.

problems.evidence: Eligibility was established across a three-month accrual window while follow-up started for everyone on a single calendar date, so the gap between the two was up to three months and was set by convenience rather than by any stated rule. The consequence is directional and large: the most informative boosted person-time is discarded at the point where waning has not yet occurred, and the reported 19% to 83% estimates are biased toward the null.
problems.quote: Similarly, if effectiveness wanes over time, delaying follow-up for up to three months unnecessarily discards the most valuable “boosted” person-time, further underestimating booster effectiveness.

problems.evidence: Surviving to the start of follow-up without a documented infection functions as an eligibility criterion applied after treatment was assigned, and it selects on an outcome-related variable during the omicron peak. Among the unboosted, passing that filter marks people with unmeasured protective behavior, so conditioning on it opens a path between treatment and outcome; the resulting selection acts in the opposite direction to the treatment effect being estimated.
problems.quote: For example, among unboosted people, the successful avoidance of SARS-CoV-2 infection during the months of peak omicron activity in the United States suggests the presence of an unmeasured protective factor (perhaps strict masking and/or social distancing).

problems.evidence: Censoring controls at booster receipt is an identifying assumption about noninformative censoring, and it was implemented as a data-handling step with no weighting and no diagnostic. Nothing in the published report distinguishes that assumption, which cannot be checked, from the matching on sex, age and comorbidity, which can, so a regulator or reader sees a single undifferentiated account of what was done.
problems.quote: the authors censored controls who received a booster during follow-up without implementing well defined statistical approaches (e.g., weighting) to mitigate selection bias likely induced by informative censoring

papers.title: Valid Evidence for Diagnosis and Treatment of Infections in the Intensive Care Unit: Beyond Randomized Control Trial Study Design (Trial Emulation and Machine Learning).
papers.one_line: A short intensive care editorial argues that trial emulation and machine learning on routine data can accelerate evidence for critically ill patients, asserting that emulation reduces bias without naming a single assumption that would have to hold.
papers.what_was_done: The piece sets out the case against relying on trials in intensive care: half of admitted patients have suspected or proven infection and 30% of them die, about 70% receive an antibiotic, and the prevalence of intensive care infection has not changed across three European prevalence surveys in 1995, 2007 and 2017. Trial cost is cited at a median 409 US dollars per recruited patient and up to 612 million dollars per trial, with recruitment slow and exclusion criteria removing the multimorbid; up to 40% of patients admitted with bleeding on a vitamin K antagonist would have been excluded from the trials supporting that indication. Observational data are then advanced as heterogeneous, cheap and able to represent combined therapies such as antibiotics with ventilation and inotropes, at the cost of confounding by indication and incomplete recording. Target trial emulation is presented as the way to raise observational quality by specifying eligibility, treatment strategies, assignment, follow-up, outcomes, causal contrast and analysis plan, and machine learning is offered as the next step, with algorithms extracting treatment rules from accumulating data. No data are analyzed and no estimate is reported.

problems.evidence: Specifying the seven protocol components is asserted to reduce bias and improve precision relative to straightforward analysis of the same data, with complexity as the only stated cost. No assumption is attached to the claim: the confounding by indication described two paragraphs earlier, where sicker intensive care patients receive combination antibiotics and closer monitoring, is untouched by writing down a protocol, yet the framework's name is what carries the credibility claim.
problems.quote: This approach reduces bias and improves the precision of estimates in contrast to the straightforward use and analysis of observational data, but it is surely more complex.

problems.evidence: Machine learning is positioned as the next level beyond observational studies, with algorithms extracting rules on which antibiotic and which supportive measures identify patients with good outcomes. Learning a rule from routine intensive care data cannot recover the treatment effect that confounding by indication has removed, and the escalation is presented as a gain in evidential strength rather than as a change in what is being estimated.
problems.quote: Applying machine learning in observational data may be the next level to observational studies.

problems.evidence: The one caveat offered is a parenthesis stating that adjustment cannot remove unmeasured confounding, set beside an unqualified claim that emulation reduces bias. Nothing distinguishes what a study could check, such as covariate balance or treatment version definitions, from what it must assume, and a reader is given no way to see which of the two applies to any particular intensive care emulation.
problems.quote: Possible confounders may be statistically adjusted (this statistical adjustment cannot remove bias and cannot remove confounding variables that are not measured)

problems.evidence: Incomplete recording, heterogeneous severity and treatment chosen by clinician experience are listed as features of routine intensive care data, and the response is that these issues matter but can be overcome by meta-analysis and statistical adjustment. No quantity of missingness or measurement failure is named at which the data would be unfit for a given question, so the assessment stays narrative.
problems.quote: Due to the heterogeneous patient population, a study may fail to detect an overall difference in treatment effects and since data are not collected comprehensively, missing data may be a problem

papers.title: Emulating Randomized Clinical Trials With Nonrandomized Real-World Evidence Studies: First Results From the RCT DUPLICATE Initiative.
papers.one_line: Ten cardiovascular trials were emulated in US claims with prospectively registered protocols and more than 120 matched confounders, and agreement was 6 of 10 on regulatory conclusion, 8 of 10 on estimate, and 9 of 10 on standardized difference, showing the verdict depends on which metric is read.
papers.what_was_done: Eight antidiabetic and two antiplatelet trials were emulated in Optum Clinformatics, IBM MarketScan and a Medicare subset using new-user cohorts, propensity score matching on more than 120 pre-exposure covariates, and protocols registered on ClinicalTrials.gov before any outcome analysis, with an audit trail in the analytics platform. Placebo arms were emulated by active comparators, dipeptidyl peptidase-4 inhibitors standing in for placebo against GLP-1 and SGLT-2 agents and second-generation sulfonylureas standing in for placebo against dipeptidyl peptidase-4 inhibitors. Three prespecified metrics were used: regulatory agreement on direction and significance, estimate agreement when the emulation hazard ratio fell inside the trial interval, and a standardized difference between estimates. Regulatory agreement held in 6 of 10, estimate agreement in 8 of 10, and only 1 of 10 exceeded a standardized difference of 2, at 3.16. Event rates were generally lower in the emulations, for example 2.0 and 2.8 per 100 person-years against 3.4 and 3.9 in LEADER, while TECOS ran higher at 7.3 and 8.3 against 4.1 and 4.2. Emulations censored at discontinuation, giving shorter follow-up than the trials' intention-to-treat analyses, and cause of death was unavailable so all recorded deaths stood in for cardiovascular death.

future_research.gap: How often and in which therapeutic contexts emulations reproduce trial findings is unknown
future_research.quote: More trial emulations are needed to understand how often and in what contexts RWE findings match RCTs.

future_research.gap: The circumstances that make agreement predictable have not been identified
future_research.quote: More evidence is needed to contribute to understanding of the circumstances that determine whether RWE findings can predictably match those of RCTs across different therapeutic areas.

problems.evidence: The same ten emulations score 6, 8 and 9 successes depending on whether the metric is regulatory conclusion, estimate containment or standardized difference, and the paper states outright that the answer varies with the metric. Worse, the metrics have known operating characteristics that were computed after the fact: estimate agreement occurs 83% of the time under no bias and 5% of emulations should exceed a standardized difference of 2 by chance, so a binary label carries almost no information about a single emulation.
problems.quote: Agreement between RCT and RWE findings varies depending on which agreement metric is used.

problems.evidence: Trials were chosen for replicability in claims: adequate power after exclusions, outcomes measurable with acceptable specificity, key confounders observable. Five antiplatelet trials were dropped for being underpowered or inpatient-only. Whatever the 6 of 10 and 8 of 10 rates measure, they were produced on a set selected for the conditions that make emulation work, and no argument connects that rate to the hypothetical questions where no trial exists, which is the stated purpose.
problems.quote: Our findings are based on a select sample of studies where RWD could emulate the outcome measure satisfactorily and key confounding factors were observable.

problems.evidence: A placebo arm cannot exist in claims, so an active drug is substituted, and the paper states this may fundamentally change the question rather than add noise. The consequence is visible: the emulations using second-generation sulfonylureas as the placebo proxy produced the largest disagreements, plausibly because cheaper sulfonylureas go to frailer and poorer patients, so the estimand became a comparison against a differently indicated drug rather than against no added treatment.
problems.quote: Close emulation of placebo is impossible via RWD, and selection of an active placebo proxy may fundamentally change the study question.

problems.evidence: Trial criteria requiring laboratory values or complete history could only be partly applied because those fields are absent from claims, and even the criteria that were applied, such as age, left distributions meaningfully different from the trials. A patient whose glycated hemoglobin was never billed is retained as if the criterion were met, which is one mechanism behind emulation cohorts that were older, more female and more likely to have heart failure than the trials they targeted.
problems.quote: Because complete health history and laboratory data were not available for all patients in the RWE, inclusion and exclusion criteria from the trials could only be partially emulated

problems.evidence: The primary endpoint in every one of the ten trials contained cardiovascular death, and claims carry no cause of death, so all recorded deaths were counted and out-of-hospital deaths were incompletely captured in the commercial databases. The endpoint phenotype therefore has both imperfect specificity and imperfect sensitivity, and its error is handled by an argument that nondifferential misclassification is conservative rather than by any measurement of the error itself.
problems.quote: counting all recorded deaths, which did not completely capture out-of-hospital deaths for the commercial claims databases used in this study

problems.evidence: The emulations censored at discontinuation while the trials analyzed by intention to treat, and the paper names nonadherence as the reason the trial estimates sit closer to the null and offers this as a partial explanation for the larger effects seen in several emulations. The two designs therefore estimate quantities that diverge as follow-up lengthens and treatment patterns converge, which the agreement metrics score as a single yes or no.
problems.quote: In contrast, the RCTs typically used an intention-to-treat approach for the primary analysis, which is known to result in effect estimates closer to the null in the context of medication nonadherence.
